finding_status.why: Replaces statistical significance rules with randomized validation samples, non-binding reference targets, iterative corrections, and a serious-harm stop rule (§3, Annex B).
Blocks future project uses and deletes controlled copies within 30 days on withdrawal while warning that existing model weights are not erased (§2 P4, Annex D).
Explicitly discloses to ASR contributors that public audio can be used to imitate or clone their voice without promising voice-identity protection (§2 P8, §3 P-A, Annex D).
Establishes a non-identifying public withdrawal list with deprecated release checksums and requires downstream users to synchronize via terms (Annex D).
Provides optional sealed contact records held by the privacy officer for lost credential recovery while prohibiting voice-matching lookups (§5 C35, Annex D).
Contracts a cultural depositary prior to retention to receive heritage collections under existing consents upon project closure (§1, §6, Annex E).
Establishes Objective 2 under an independent institutional host and cultural depositary with its own budget line and month-18 funding plan (§1, §5 K02, §6).
Constitutes an interim community-majority council at M0 with defined quorum rules and caps non-veto disputes at 30 days before independent reviewer decision (§5 K02).
Keeps mixed MSA/Lebanese programmes in scope with four evaluation criteria, but leaves thresholds and definitions unspecified and pending owner approval (§4 C-B).
Mandates single-pass capture of endangered carriers during audit and relies on human sampling for programme-level language auditing (§4 C-B).
Removes the conditional gate on private synthesis, allowing it to proceed by owner decision sized to K30 needs and third-party comparisons (§3 K07).
Separates secure storage verification at G-1 from private synthesis compute, location, access, and isolation verification at G-3 (§5, Annex A).
Requires filing Law 81/2018 declarations, including Article 96(12) foreign transfers, before collection and as a condition of Gate G-1 (§5, Annex A).
Excludes individuals with failed comprehension or doubtful capacity from public ASR while permitting companion-supported heritage participation (§5 C35, Annex E).
Digitizes household broadcast recordings solely to preserve originals and withholds replacement copies pending counsel's opinion on third-party copying (§4 C-C, §5).
Requires reviewing applicable diaspora privacy jurisdictions and retaining impact assessments and transfer safeguards prior to Gate G-1 (§5, Annex A).
Body remains ~1,674 words against the 1,600-word limit despite claiming duplicated reasoning was trimmed (§7).

new_problems.name: Pre-G-1 recording trials conflict with Law 81/2018
new_problems.problem: Section 5 requires filed Law 81/2018 declarations 'before collection', whereas Annex A allows 'non-retained trials only' prior to G-1 declaration verification. Recording live human speech during pre-G-1 trials still constitutes personal data processing without prior declaration.
new_problems.fix: Amend Annex A (G-1) to specify that pre-G-1 trials may only use pre-existing public/synthetic audio, or require Law 81/2018 filing prior to any live speaker recording.

support.claim: Law 81/2018 requires prior declaration covering personal data processing and foreign transfers.
support.fragment: «عند الاقتضاء، نقل البيانات ذات الطابع الشخصي الى دولة اخرى في اي شكل كان»

support.claim: Recording human voices for trials is personal data collection regardless of later deletion.
premises: Section 5 mandates filed declarations before collection.
Annex A permits non-retained trials before G-1 verifies the filed declaration.

new_problems.name: Ethics approval scheduled concurrently with pilot execution
new_problems.problem: Annex A requires research ethics committee approval 'before their implementation and G-2' for K30 randomization and P-A collection, but Section 6 schedules 'Ethics approval, pilot, G-2' together in M3–6 without explicitly gating the pilot start.
new_problems.fix: Move ethics committee approval into M0–3 in Section 6, explicitly preceding any K30 randomization or P-A pilot recruitment.

support.claim: Ethics review cannot occur concurrently with the human-subjects pilot it is meant to authorize.
premises: Annex A states ethics approval must occur before K30 randomization and P-A collection implementation.
Section 6 places ethics approval and the pilot in the same M3–6 window.

new_problems.name: Private synthesis withdrawal leaves active voice persona deployed
new_problems.problem: Private synthesis relies on 'few selected voices' (§3 P-A), yet Annex D states existing model weights need not be erased upon withdrawal without requiring retirement of that contributor's synthetic voice persona from K30 service.
new_problems.fix: Add to Annex D that if a private-synthesis voice contributor withdraws, their specific voice persona/adapter is retired from active K30 synthesis deployment within 30 days.

support.claim: Continuing to generate speech in a withdrawn studio actor's voice violates the rule stopping future project uses.
premises: Annex D blocks all future project uses upon withdrawal.
Private synthesis uses a small, identifiable set of studio voices rather than diffuse crowd averages.

new_problems.name: Unverified statutory bases for 50-year broadcast triage
new_problems.problem: Programme C-B treats 'broadcasts older than 50 years' as a primary rights-triage category while Section 5 notes 50 years alone does not establish unrestricted reuse, and Annex G confirms the statutory fragment (S10) was not verified.
new_problems.fix: Label the 50-year triage bucket provisional pending counsel verification of Lebanese copyright/neighboring-rights terms before any C-C rebroadcasting.

support.claim: Operational triage buckets should not rely on unverified statutory durations.
premises: Annex G (S10) marks the 50-year broadcaster term as unretrieved and pending counsel confirmation.
Section 5 already warns that 50 years does not clear underlying works or performers.

new_problems.name: Body text exceeds mandatory 1,600-word ceiling
new_problems.problem: The strategy body is approximately 1,674 words, violating the 1,600-word limit due to repeated withdrawal, closure, and gate rules across §§2, 5, and 6 that already appear in Annexes A–E.
new_problems.fix: Cut ~85 words of duplicated operational detail from §§5–6 by cross-referencing Annexes A, D, and E.

support.claim: Trimming redundant cross-references brings the document within the 1,600-word limit without losing substance.
premises: Verifier count shows ~1,674 body words against a 1,600-word limit.
Withdrawal timelines and closure transfer steps are stated in full in both the main body and Annexes D–E.

pertinence_parameters.assessment: Useful as high-level triage dimensions for prioritizing mixed MSA/Lebanese programmes, but not yet actionable because they lack quantitative cutoffs, scoring weights, and segment-level handling rules.
missing: Minimum Lebanese speech share threshold (e.g., percentage of programme runtime or spoken turns) required for inclusion
Operational rubric defining 'cultural value' (e.g., endangered regional dialect, oral poetry, occupational lexicon, or historical uniqueness)
Definition of 'separability' and policy on whether interspersed MSA segments are retained in context or excised during archival preservation
Carrier-condition triage matrix linking physical degradation urgency to capture priority
Owner approval deadline and default interim rule so C-B audits are not stalled waiting for sign-off

verdict_reason: Strategy v4.1 faithfully implements nearly all owner dispositions, cleanly separating cultural preservation from AI gates and replacing rigid statistical rules with iterative validation. Adopt once five targeted fixes are applied: trim ~85 body words to meet the 1,600-word cap, align pre-G-1 trial and ethics sequencing with Law 81/2018, retire withdrawn synthesis personas, and operationalize mixed-programme thresholds.
